content: 1. Inhibitors of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters can elevate the concentration and toxicity of drugs that are substrates of these transporters. 2. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase erythromycin base levels or effects through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised during coadministration. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3. This interaction necessitates careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments. 4. Eslicarbazepine acetate reduces the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Drugs that induce CYP3A4, such as eslicarbazepine acetate, may decrease plasma concentrations of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, potentially reducing its therapeutic efficacy. Monitoring and dose adjustments may be required. 6. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of estradiol, etoposide, and other drugs by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 8. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of everolimus, ezetimibe, and other drugs by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter or other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are required. 9. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 10. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Flibanserin increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is advised. 12. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases fluvastatin levels, which may elevate the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis, due to OATP1B1 inhibition. The lowest approved dose of fluvastatin should be used, and higher doses should be carefully assessed for risk versus benefit. 13.
